actions.added_meaning: Selected exact House 110019 death/disability loan-discharge income-exclusion and SSN provisions follow. House 110019 exclusion grounds: In the case of an individual, gross income does not include any amount which (but for this subsection) would be includible in gross income for such taxable year by reason of the discharge (in whole or in part) of any loan described in subparagraph (B), if such discharge was-- (i) pursuant to subsection (a) or (d) of section 437 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 or the parallel benefit under part D of title IV of such Act (relating to the repayment of loan liability), (ii) pursuant to section 464(c)(1)(F) of such Act, or (iii) otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. House 110019 loan categories: A loan is described in this subparagraph if such loan is-- (i) a student loan (as defined in paragraph (2)), or (ii) a private education loan (as defined in section 140(a) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 1650(a)). House 110019 identification and own marital rules: (i) In general.--Subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to any discharge during any taxable year unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for such taxable year-- (I) the taxpayer's social security number, and (II) if the taxpayer is married, the social security number of such taxpayers's spouse. (ii) Social security number.--For purposes of this subparagraph, the term `social security number' has the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). (iii) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this subparagraph.. House 110019 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2) is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (U), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (V) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (V) the following new subparagraph: (W) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 108(f)(5)(C) (relating to discharges on account of death or disability).. House 110019 discharge-date applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to discharges after December 31, 2025. Each version replaces only 108(f)(5) with the printed exclusion, not all of section 108 or every student-loan tax rule. The original 2024 (5) instead covers its defined discharge categories after December 31, 2020 and before January 1, 2026; the candidate does not silently extend that entire temporary rule unchanged. The common requirement that the discharged loan meet new subparagraph (B) applies across all three ground alternatives. Interaction of that gate, complete loan definitions and the parent-borrower 437(d) reference is reserved as question 55; no blanket conclusion that every HEA discharge qualifies for tax exclusion. Original (f)(1) service-conditioned discharge and (4) named repayment-program exclusions remain separate. New loan categories retain full 108(f)(2) student-loan definition and entire 140(a) private-education definitions, including actual (a)(8) private loan, own private-lender and expense meanings and excluded credit/mortgage categories. This does not mean every education-related debt qualifies. The three exclusion-ground alternatives remain separate: the first two use their specified HEA discharge paths, while only the third prints otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. A parent borrower is not silently equated to the student. Full 437(a) retains qualifying loans, death/disability determinations, safeguards, conditional reinstatement, VA documentation and own income-monitoring/approval/opt-out/update rules; 437(d) separately addresses a parent loan when the student dies. Captured 464(c)(1)(F) retains loan-fund agreement scope, borrower death, regulated permanent/total disability, the medically determinable substantial-gainful-activity alternative with its own duration/death tests, and VA unemployability due to service-connected disability. Part D parallel benefit is retained with complete captured 455 and its unless-otherwise-specified limitation, not a universal cancellation promise. Tax exclusion after a qualifying discharge is distinct from authority to cancel a loan. Both versions define the SSN by 24(h)(7), with their own same-bill amended definition and previously bound SSA issuance authority: citizen or the specified authorization route, and issuance before the return due date, not a bare identification number or a citizen-only rule. No child-credit amount or qualifying-child requirement is imported into the loan exclusion. Math-error treatment retains the existing notice and conditional abatement/deficiency procedure, including the 60-day abatement-request path; it is not a fraud finding or actual assessment. The effective date is discharges after December 31, 2025, not taxable years beginning after that date. No individual exclusion, discharge, marital status, SSA-number validity or return result is inferred. House adds both taxpayer and, if married, spouse SSNs on the return, and rules similar to 32(d). The complete captured 32(d) joint-return default and separated-spouse exception retain all their own conjunctions, qualifying-child residence and alternative abode/decree/household conditions as context, not an automatically transposed universal filing or child duty. This House-specific application remains reserved as question 54. House inserts math-error subparagraph (W). Other H.R.1 components and all separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.

actions.added_meaning: Selected exact Senate 70119 death/disability loan-discharge income-exclusion and SSN provisions follow. Senate 70119 exclusion grounds: In the case of an individual, gross income does not include any amount which (but for this subsection) would be includible in gross income for such taxable year by reason of the discharge (in whole or in part) of any loan described in subparagraph (B), if such discharge was-- (i) pursuant to subsection (a) or (d) of section 437 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 or the parallel benefit under part D of title IV of such Act (relating to the repayment of loan liability), (ii) pursuant to section 464(c)(1)(F) of such Act, or (iii) otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. Senate 70119 loan categories: A loan is described in this subparagraph if such loan is-- (i) a student loan (as defined in paragraph (2)), or (ii) a private education loan (as defined in section 140(a) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 1650(a)). Senate 70119 identification and own marital rules: (i) In general.--Subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to any discharge during any taxable year unless the taxpayer includes the taxpayer's social security number on the return of tax for such taxable year. (ii) Social security number.--For purposes of this subparagraph, the term `social security number' has the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. Senate 70119 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by this Act, is further amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (V), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (W) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (W) the following new subparagraph: (X) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 108(f)(5)(C) (relating to discharges on account of death or disability).. Senate 70119 discharge-date applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to discharges after December 31, 2025. Each version replaces only 108(f)(5) with the printed exclusion, not all of section 108 or every student-loan tax rule. The original 2024 (5) instead covers its defined discharge categories after December 31, 2020 and before January 1, 2026; the candidate does not silently extend that entire temporary rule unchanged. The common requirement that the discharged loan meet new subparagraph (B) applies across all three ground alternatives. Interaction of that gate, complete loan definitions and the parent-borrower 437(d) reference is reserved as question 55; no blanket conclusion that every HEA discharge qualifies for tax exclusion. Original (f)(1) service-conditioned discharge and (4) named repayment-program exclusions remain separate. New loan categories retain full 108(f)(2) student-loan definition and entire 140(a) private-education definitions, including actual (a)(8) private loan, own private-lender and expense meanings and excluded credit/mortgage categories. This does not mean every education-related debt qualifies. The three exclusion-ground alternatives remain separate: the first two use their specified HEA discharge paths, while only the third prints otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. A parent borrower is not silently equated to the student. Full 437(a) retains qualifying loans, death/disability determinations, safeguards, conditional reinstatement, VA documentation and own income-monitoring/approval/opt-out/update rules; 437(d) separately addresses a parent loan when the student dies. Captured 464(c)(1)(F) retains loan-fund agreement scope, borrower death, regulated permanent/total disability, the medically determinable substantial-gainful-activity alternative with its own duration/death tests, and VA unemployability due to service-connected disability. Part D parallel benefit is retained with complete captured 455 and its unless-otherwise-specified limitation, not a universal cancellation promise. Tax exclusion after a qualifying discharge is distinct from authority to cancel a loan. Both versions define the SSN by 24(h)(7), with their own same-bill amended definition and previously bound SSA issuance authority: citizen or the specified authorization route, and issuance before the return due date, not a bare identification number or a citizen-only rule. No child-credit amount or qualifying-child requirement is imported into the loan exclusion. Math-error treatment retains the existing notice and conditional abatement/deficiency procedure, including the 60-day abatement-request path; it is not a fraud finding or actual assessment. The effective date is discharges after December 31, 2025, not taxable years beginning after that date. No individual exclusion, discharge, marital status, SSA-number validity or return result is inferred. Senate requires the taxpayer SSN on the return and does not print the House conditional-spouse requirement or similar-32(d) addition. Those House clauses are not borrowed. Senate further amends the as-amended math-error list by adding (X), not House (W). House application question 54 is not treated as a settled Senate marital rule. Other H.R.1 components and all separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
